In particular, we cannot derive the structure of the source in detail, nor do we have the sensitivity at high resolution needed for investigation of detailed structure within the mass model.

all_quotes.loc: 3.1.2 ALMA observations: velocity-resolved structure in the CO(5-4) line
all_quotes.quote: while we may be tempted to interpret the source to be a warped disk, it should be noted that there could be a large error bar on the fit to the velocity planes towards the red end because of their low signal to noise

Even though the median size of the radio source inferred from the u − v fit is seen to be only 1.3σ away from zero, it can be seen from Figure 8 that the radio data is inconsistent with a point source. We also find that the radio source size is sensitive to the starting parameters of the u − v fit optimisation.

all_quotes.loc: 4.1 The radio source and the CO(5-4) line
all_quotes.quote: Whether the radio emission contains partial contribution from an AGN-type source, as in HS 0810+2554 (Hartley et al. 2019) will be interesting to determine from future VLBI observations.
The observation was made under proposal code AJ413 (PI Jackson) in the C-band (4.488–6.512 GHz) with a total bandwidth of 2 GHz using 16 IFs of 128 MHz each.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA2018.1.01447.S.
